El Mamo Camilo shared with us their duty to preserve the "heart of the Earth." He believes, "By keeping Nature at the forefront of our thoughts, we can breathe clean air, be free from viruses, and lead healthy lives." He sees hope in our growing unity and in giving them a stronger voice than ever before. The story of cacao speaks to the conservation and rejuvenation of their sacred sites to maintain a balanced Nature. Spreading this message of protecting Mother Nature between two brothers signifies healing in both the physical and spiritual realms. This ensures that animals, rivers, mountains, glaciers, and the air remain enduring. By sharing this message, perhaps through this chocolate, your support will aid us in healing the planet. I hope you savor the richness of this extra dark milk chocolate, enhanced by the crunch of the Arhuacos' roasted cacao. -Denise Castronovo

I learned about a cacao cooperative of indigenous women from the Awajún and Huambisa communities in the Amazon rainforest. Traditionally, men provide for their families by selling their hunt and fish catch for income and women take care of farming, cooking, and the children. Now, with the commercialization of cacao women are rapidly becoming empowered and the breadwinners for the family. Government-funded cacao projects are helping them succeed. Quality cacao has enabled new schools and health centers, better education, and higher income. Your purchase helps facilitate their progress and protects the Amazon rainforest. Enjoy the rich chocolate flavors from this rainforest cacao that are laced with natural sweet flavors of almond, vanilla and caramel. -Denise Castronovo, Chocolate Maker

Front-of-pack text (as printed): Castronovo® CHOCOLATE — CACAO FRUIT — WHITE CHOCOLATE — 2.2 oz | 62 g
Full description (EN): Cacao Fruit white chocolate. When I visit cacao farms in search of rare cacao, my journey begins with the fruit itself. I smell and taste the pulp of each variety growing on the land, because that is where the true flavor potential lies. During fermentation, the fruit's vibrant essence infuses into the seeds, shaping the complexity of the final chocolate. The ritual of tasting fresh cacao pulp is rarely experienced by chocolate lovers. It begins with the farmer selecting a ripe pod with a machete, slicing it open just a crack to smell its fleeting aroma before sharing the seeds. With up to 30 per pod, each tasting becomes communal. Each cacao variety surprises your palate with tropical flavors, some unlike anything you've ever tasted. And then comes the moment of wonder... biting into a seed and discovering - did I get a rare, white cacao seed? This white chocolate infused with Peruvian, Piura Blanco cacao pulp brings the farm to you. It's a glimpse into the heart of cacao. -Denise Castronovo, Chocolate Maker

Front-of-pack text (as printed): Castronovo® CHOCOLATE — 2020 Harvest — CHUAO — VENEZUELA — 72% Dark Chocolate — 2.2 oz | 62 g
Full description (EN): Nestled in the valley of the cloud forest, lies the isolated village of Chuao in Venezuela. Only reachable by boat or on foot through the jungle, the village takes you away from the modern world to a setting of overwhelming nature and a 400-year tradition of cacao production, carried out by its native African American residents. Chuao's last-surviving, aristocratic Spanish heir, Doña Catalina, gifted the plantation and her slaves to the Franciscan friars, who erected Chuao's iconic church, cacao drying patio, processing area, and a place for social and cultural gathering. In the 1960s, historical justice arose from the valley when the workers were given the farm. Today only descendents of the original slaves, mostly women, work the cacao plantation. The women sing while they work, "long live the Chuao cacao, founded by Doña Catalina, it's rich and tasty and harvested by all of us."

Cacao variety: criollo (inferred from story: 'pure Mesoamerican criollo cacao' brought in 1670)
Tasting notes (EN): cashew, banana, vanilla, milk, toffee; minimal acidity and bitterness (from description)
Full description (EN):
Recently, my interest was piqued by the historical journey of cacao, originating in the northwest Amazon and spreading globally. Pure criollo cacao likely traversed from coastal Peru to Mesoamerica via the Pacific Ocean, where it was enjoyed by the Mokaya, Olmec, Maya, and Aztec civilizations before being introduced to the Spanish. In 1670, the Spanish brought pure Mesoamerican criollo cacao to the Philippines through the Acapulco-Manila trade route.

Inspired by this rich history, I made a microbatch of chocolate from Kablon Farms cacao. I love its exquisite aroma and sweet, nutty flavors reminiscent of cashew, banana, vanilla, milk, toffee, with minimal acidity and bitterness in a dark chocolate. My limited release chocolate aims to showcase its unique flavor profile, distinct from my usual Latin American origins. Moreover, highlighting the Philippines, a global biodiversity hotspot in need of conservation, adds further significance to this endeavor. -Denise Castronovo, Chocolate Maker

Front-of-pack text (as printed): Castronovo Chocolate — Piura Blanco — Piura, Peru — Dark Chocolate 76% — 2.2 oz | 62 g
Tasting notes (EN): natural citric acidity reminiscent of starfruit, with a soft nuttiness of almond; delicate, creamy and mild pulp
Full description (EN): Piura Blanco, PIURA, PERU. After six years, I returned to the Cacao and Chocolate Salon in Lima, Peru, on a mission: to find the most extraordinary cacao for you. I tasted my way through countless origins, but one stood out - a rare heirloom cacao from the Piura Valley, known for its white seeds and low tannins. The cacao is unlike any other. It is the only variety that thrives in the desert climate, where the dry conditions concentrate its fruity flavors. When I tasted its cacao pulp it was so delicate, creamy and mild. Roasting this cacao requires precision. I've developed a technique that balances its natural citric acidity, reminiscent of starfruit, with a soft nuttiness of almond. This careful approach allows me to use less sugar, creating a chocolate that's both healthier and bitter-free. I invite you to savor this chocolate that is vibrant, nuanced, and satisfying. Try it with fresh oranges, almonds, a crisp white wine or Grand Marnier. -Denise Castronovo, Chocolate Maker

Full description (EN): Piura Blanco, PIURA, PERU. After six years, I returned to the Cacao and Chocolate Salon in Lima, Peru, on a mission: to find the most extraordinary cacao for you. I tasted my way through countless origins, but one stood out - a rare heirloom cacao from the Piura Valley, known for its white seeds and low tannins. The cacao is unlike any other. It is the only variety that thrives in the desert climate, where the dry conditions concentrate its fruity flavors. When I tasted its cacao pulp it was so delicate, creamy and mild. Roasting this cacao requires precision. I've developed a technique that balances its natural citric acidity, reminiscent of starfruit, with a soft nuttiness of almond. This careful approach allows me to use less sugar, creating a chocolate that's both healthier and bitter-free. I invite you to savor this chocolate that is vibrant, nuanced, and satisfying. Try it with fresh oranges, almonds, a crisp white wine or Grand Marnier. -Denise Castronovo, Chocolate Maker

Tasting notes (EN): delicate floral, vanilla, and soft tropical fruit flavors
Full description (EN): In the 1600's most of Puerto Rico was planted in cacao by the Spanish. It was an important export to Europe until a hurricane forced its abandonment. On their farm, our partners Juan and Maria have original trees. In the aftermath of Hurricane Maria 2017, they are still restoring their farm. It turns out that the old trees are more resilient and produced the majority of their harvest. Juan and Maria are dedicated to developing the fine cocoa industry in Puerto Rico with our cooperation. The cacao has a natural sweetness which brings delicate floral, vanilla, and soft tropical fruit flavors to our chocolate.

Full description (EN): In 2019, I was invited to Peru to represent U.S. chocolate makers at the Cacao and Chocolate Salon in Lima. I learned about an interesting mix of native criollo cacao from the northern coastal desert region of Piura. Typically cacao is native to the rainforest, but this cacao has adapted to the dry, arid environment at the lowest point of the Andes where the Amazon meets the desert coast. Knowing that a drier climate imparts nice flavors in cacao and fewer tannins, I wanted to make a chocolate out of this variety for you to taste. This chocolate boasts bright citrus and tropical fruit flavors up front that transition to delicate nutty and spice flavors at its finish, intriguing you to try another piece. That unforgettable moment inspired this bar - a celebration of Peru's lively character, infused with real tangerine to recreate the joy of that pairing. Bright, balanced, and beautifully nuanced, it's a taste journey I am thrilled to share with you. -Denise Castronovo, Chocolate Maker

Full description (EN): We sort, roast, crack, winnow, grind, and conch small batches of beans. Then we temper, mold, and wrap each bar in gold foil and recycled cotton paper. Tasting notes (EN): raisin, fig, chocolate cake, walnuts, vanilla
Full description (EN): The cacao beans used to make this chocolate is grown by 500 smallholder farmers in the lush growing region of Bundibugyo in Uganda. Each farm is 1-2 hectares, either owned as family land or leased from other farmers. Wet beans are bought and transferred to a central post harvest facility in a converted B&B in the village of Bumate. The location is at the base of the hills leading into the mountains taking advantage of maximum sunshine and limiting runoff. This chocolate bar is community supported. Chocolatemakers are given an opportunity to pay a bonus per kg to be used directly to support the farmers that make Semuliki Forest cacao possible. This year the fund will be used to pay school fees for the farmer's children.
